title: Checkout retries
summary: Retry transient payment-gateway failures with an idempotency key derived from the order id. About 2% of gateway calls fail transiently and every one is surfaced to the customer today. The cost is one reconciliation job and a flag.
motivation: Payment gateway calls fail transiently about 2% of the time; each failure is shown to the customer as a declined checkout, and support sees roughly forty tickets a week that are retries done by hand.
goals: Retry transient gateway failures without duplicating charges.
proposal: Wrap the gateway client in an idempotent retry: three attempts, exponential backoff capped at 800 ms, with an idempotency key derived from the order id so a retried request that already succeeded is a no-op at the gateway. The wrapper is behind a flag and logs every retry with the attempt number and the gateway's response code.

alternatives.name: Client-side retry in the web app
alternatives.whyNot: duplicates charges when the first call succeeded but the response was lost; the browser has no idempotency key.

alternatives.name: Queue and reconcile asynchronously
alternatives.whyNot: correct, but moves checkout off the request path and changes the customer experience for every order to fix 2% of them.

risks.risk: The gateway ignores the idempotency key in one region
risks.mitigation: a reconciliation job voids duplicate captures within five minutes; verified against the sandbox for both regions before rollout.

rollout.plan: Behind a flag: 1% of traffic for one day, then 25%, then 100%, watching duplicate-capture and p99 dashboards at each step.
rollout.rollback: flip the flag off; no data migration is involved.
